latest_findings.claim: At N=256 and 6000 steps, force did not stay flat, and it does not look like a ceiling either. Seed 20's force margin went from 0.102 at step 3000 to 0.139 at step 6000 (layer 1, R2 0.670 vs control 0.531; it first crossed the 0.1 bar at step 3000). Seed 21's went from 0.001 to 0.044 (R2 0.624 vs control 0.580), rising about +0.007 to +0.010 per 500 steps after it moved to layer 1 at step 3500. Both seeds were still rising at step 6000. accel_step behaved as predicted: its margin stayed flat (0.201 to 0.205 for seed 21, 0.158 to 0.163 for seed 20), giving headroom-normalized margins of 0.72 and 0.69, against 0.10 and 0.30 for force.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither the if-true nor the if-false outcome happened. The ceiling prediction needed a final force margin < 0.10 and a gain of <= 0.03 in both seeds. Seed 20 ended at 0.139, and both gains were above 0.03 (0.037 and 0.043). The if-false outcome needed a final margin >= 0.12 in both seeds or a gain of >= 0.06 in both. Seed 21 ended at 0.044, and neither gain reached 0.06. The accel_step half of the hypothesis held in both seeds, with normalized margins of 0.69 and 0.72, inside [0.62, 0.77]. The trajectories argue against a hard ceiling. Force was still climbing at step 6000 in both seeds, and the 3000-to-6000 gains here (0.037-0.043) are larger than at N=128 in the paired arm (0.022-0.031). That points to a later or slower start rather than a lower limit, but two seeds that disagree by about 0.1 can't settle it. Two things complicate the comparison with earlier work. First, the step-3000 force margins here (0.102 and 0.001) both differ from the 0.033-0.040 reported for the earlier 3000-step N=256 runs, so nondeterminism or an lr-schedule-horizon effect is still possible. Second, seed 21's force control_spread (0.054) is larger than seed 20's (0.025). Both runs completed all 6000 steps, and val_mse_ratio fell to 0.10-0.12, below 1 from step 3000 on. The verdict would become refuted if 12000-step runs took both seeds' force margin to >= 0.12. It would become supported if both levelled off below 0.10, or if a rerun showed that seed 20's step-3000 value of 0.102 is a nondeterministic outlier.

latest_findings.claim: At N=128 with training doubled to 6000 steps, the force margin was still rising slowly and did not reach the N=64 band (0.21-0.26). It ended at 0.178 for seed 20 (layer 1; R2 0.670 vs control 0.492) and 0.163 for seed 21 (best layer moving among 1, 2 and 4; R2 0.629 vs control 0.466). The gains from step 3000 to 6000 were +0.031 and +0.022, and neither curve has levelled off: the last 1000 steps added +0.009 and +0.007. accel_step was flat throughout, with margins 0.151 and 0.170 and headroom-normalised margins of about 0.70 in both seeds (R2 0.934 vs control 0.783; 0.927 vs 0.757). That fits the expected [0.62, 0.77] range. Normalised force margins were only 0.35 and 0.31, so on both raw and normalised margin accel_step leads force.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither pre-registered outcome happened. The supported case needed a final margin >= 0.20 and a gain >= 0.04 in both seeds; both seeds fall short on both. The refuted case needed a final margin <= 0.17 and a gain <= 0.02 in both seeds. Seed 20 ends at 0.178 with a +0.031 gain, and seed 21's gain of +0.022 is just over the 0.02 limit. The result is a third pattern the hypothesis did not set out: steady growth of about 0.004-0.005 per 500 steps, with no plateau and no catch-up. Over the same span val_mse_ratio fell 5-9x (0.24/0.14 at step 3000 to 0.027/0.030 at step 6000). The step-3000 checkpoints match the earlier 3000-step runs to within 0.003 (seed 20: 0.147 vs 0.150) and 0.010 (seed 21: 0.141 vs 0.131). That is under the 0.03 rule, so cross-run comparison is valid and the lr-schedule horizon has little visible effect at N=128. Both runs completed 6000/6000 steps, and checkpoints were every 500 steps. If growth stays linear, seed 20 would reach 0.20 at roughly 8000-9000 steps and seed 21 at roughly 10000-11000. A 12000-step run would separate 'slower growth' from 'lower ceiling'. The verdict would change to supported if force reached >= 0.20 in both seeds by then, and to refuted if both levelled off below 0.18. With only two seeds, and seed 21's best force layer changing between checkpoints (likely a flat per-layer profile), the per-seed numbers are noisy at the 0.01-0.02 level.

latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 1 (N=64, e<=0.5, 4 layers, d_model=64), training to 1500 steps makes force beat its best-of-5 control persistently in all 3 seeds. Read from the trajectories, force first holds >= 0.1 at step 400 (seed 75), 450 (seed 77) and 600 (seed 76), and ends at margins 0.196, 0.193 and 0.167 (R2 0.738/0.718/0.684 vs controls 0.542/0.525/0.517). accel_step stays roughly flat: it gains 0.006-0.018 after step 600 and ends at 0.156/0.160/0.177 (R2 0.92-0.93 vs controls 0.75-0.77). Headroom-normalised, accel_step still leads force in every seed (0.66-0.71 vs 0.35-0.43).
latest_findings.confidence_note: All three predictions held: force formed persistently by step 1500 in 3 of 3 seeds, final force margin was >= 0.11 in each, and accel_step moved less than 0.03 from its step-600 value. All runs completed 1500 of 1500 steps, the force control_spread (0.030-0.061) is below the 0.1 bar, and the controls differ by under 0.03 across seeds, so the margins are not control noise. Three caveats limit what this means. (1) In these 1500-step runs, force margin at step 600 is already 0.104-0.138, but the 600-step runs with the same seeds and data were at 0.085-0.099. The original 'no force code' null was therefore partly an artefact of where training stopped or of the lr schedule horizon, not only of total step count. (2) Force only crosses the bar after its best layer moves from 4 to 1 (the distance layer, distance margin 0.47-0.66) at steps 250-400. Layer-4 force never exceeds about 0.085. So this force signal may be a nonlinear read of distance and orbit scale rather than an m2-weighted force. Regressing distance and accel_step out of the force target would change the interpretation, though not this verdict. (3) Force is still rising at step 1500 (+0.002-0.004 per 50 steps), so the final margin is not a ceiling. The verdict would flip only if a rerun of this exact config failed to cross the bar.

latest_findings.claim: With data_seed 1, both fresh seeds reproduce the late-forming, late-strengthening force code seen on data_seed 0 (4 layers, d_model=128, N=64, e<=0.5, 5000 steps, best-of-5 controls). Final force margins are 0.187 (seed 79, R2 0.809 vs control 0.623) and 0.208 (seed 80, R2 0.817 vs control 0.608). Persistent force formation comes at steps 400 and 350, against step 100 for accel_step in both seeds, a lag of 300 and 250 steps. From step 500 to 5000, force gains +0.074 and +0.081 while accel_step gains only +0.025 and +0.022. accel_step still has the larger raw margin (0.165 and 0.191; R2 0.974 vs control 0.809, and 0.960 vs 0.769) and the larger headroom-normalised margin (0.86 and 0.83, vs 0.49 and 0.53 for force).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds finished all 5000 steps and pass every expected-if-true criterion by a clear margin, so the pattern does not depend on the dataset. On this data_seed the force margins are slightly lower than on data_seed 0 (0.187-0.208 vs 0.21-0.23). Persistent formation steps were read from the trajectory with a strict >= 0.1 bar, and here they match probes_final.formed_at_step. Force control_spread is 0.027-0.028, so the bar stays at 0.1. Four limits apply. (1) Force has not been residualised against distance or accel_step. Its late gain runs alongside the fall in val_mse_ratio (about 0.27-0.41 at step 500 to 0.005-0.006 at step 5000), so it could be a sharpening read of the distance or accel_step code rather than a separate m2-weighted force feature. (2) The layer carrying force is not stable: in seed 79 the best layer moves from 4 to 1 at step 400 and back to 4 at step 2000, while seed 80 stays at layer 4 throughout. (3) Only two data_seeds have been tested. (4) Random controls at d_model=128 are high (0.61-0.62 for force, 0.76-0.81 for accel_step and distance), which squeezes the raw margins. What would change the verdict: if the force margin drops below 0.1 once accel_step and distance are regressed out of the force target, the late force code is a derived read rather than a force representation.

latest_findings.claim: At N=128 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the final force margin is in between the other arms in both seeds: 0.150 (seed 20, R2 0.642 vs control 0.492, layer 1) and 0.131 (seed 21, R2 0.603 vs 0.472, layer 1). That is below N=64 (0.21-0.26) and above N=256 (0.03-0.04), so force falls by roughly 0.1 per doubling of N, a gradual decline in log N. accel_step margins are 0.151/0.163 (R2 0.934/0.920 at layer 4, controls 0.783/0.757), with headroom-normalized margins of 0.70/0.67. The accel_step control did not fall from its N=64 level (0.77-0.79), and seed 20's 0.783 is just outside the predicted [0.66, 0.78] band.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The main force prediction holds in both seeds: final margins of 0.150 and 0.131 sit inside [0.08, 0.19] and clear of both falsifying bands. Normalized accel_step (0.70/0.67) is inside [0.62, 0.77]. The verdict is not 'supported' because one stated criterion fails narrowly: seed 20's accel_step control R2 is 0.7826, above the 0.78 upper bound. The hypothesis's mechanism also fails. It said the accel_step control would fall between N=64 and N=256 alongside force, but at N=128 the control (0.757-0.783) matches N=64, while force has already lost about 0.1 of margin. The force decline therefore does not move with the accel_step control. The force control (0.47-0.49) is also flat against N=64 (0.48-0.51) and N=256 (~0.5). Both runs are complete (3000/3000 steps) and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.069-0.071). Force had not levelled off at step 3000: it gained +0.006 (seed 20) and +0.004 (seed 21) over the last 500 steps. The N=128 value may therefore partly reflect slower force growth rather than a lower ceiling, and longer training could move it toward the N=64 band. Formation steps read from the trajectories match formed_at_step (force persistent from 1000 in seed 20 and 1500 in seed 21; accel_step from 500 in both). Seed 21's force best layer switched from 4 to 1 only at step 3000. Each arm has only 2 seeds and one data_seed. The verdict would become 'supported' if the band were judged at 2-decimal precision. It would become 'refuted' for the mechanism if added seeds kept the N=128 accel_step control at N=64 levels.
